newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares ease at close as earnings concerns bite.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares ease at close as earnings concerns bite.

text.p: * Telecom, CHH lead NZ market lower at close
* Wrightson gains despite bad news on earnings front
* Cultus soars after Australian progress report
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
337 -3 * NZSC cap index -8.90 at 5,106.28
286 -1 * NZSE-10 cap index -8.51 at 1,195.55 375 +1 * Volume NZ$63 million. Futures -14 at 1,198
738 -6 * Other movers - +50 +4
Drops in most leading stocks took New Zealand shares lower at the close on Friday as concerns about the corporate earnings outlook started to bite.
By the close, the NZSE-40 Capital Index was down 13.76 at 2,386.74. On the surface, turnover looked high at NZ$63 million, but much of that was restricted to crossings in isolated stocks.

Rumours regarding a takeover of Lion Nathan were beginning to fade, but the stock still attracted high turnover, with 1.58 million shares (worth NZ$5.9 million) trading. Lion was also the only leading issue to gain, adding one to NZ$3.75.
The main mover, Telecom, lost six to NZ$7.38 but was still within its recent NZ$7.20-7.50 trading range. Brokers said there was a suggestion of some earnings downgrades in the market.
John Rattray at Ord Minnett said the market's losses were trimmed towards the end of the session.
"There is no particular theme or tone but we are into this late January-February market and the seasonality would suggest the market is going to struggle," Rattray said.
"The earnings profiles and the earnings outturns suggest that corporate New Zealand is struggling.

"Interest rates and the currency will still gnaw away at it a bit," he said. "I think it's a bit of a battle at the moment and it will remain subdued. It's lost any responsiveness to any international forces and the domestic economy is a difficult place for those who are out there at the moment. I think the share market is a good reflector of that," he said.

Farm services group Wrightson actually gained four cents to close at NZ$1.09 on high turnover, despite earlier advising the market that its 1996/97 profit would be significantly below the forecast range.
But Wrightson had come a long way down from around NZ$1.22 at the start of the year as concerns about the rural downturn grew, and today's move was seen as a bounce-back.
Outside the leading issues, Cultus Petroleum -- 30 percent owned by Auckland merchant bankers Sir Michael Fay and David Richwhite -- gained 50 cents to NZ$2.00, a high for the year.
Both Australian and New Zealand markets re-rated Cultus on the strength of latest results from the Cornea wells, offshore Western Australia, which the company said were positive.
